tests.name: Energy Stores & Transfers
tests.description: Identify energy stores and calculate basic energy values

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an energy store?
questions.explanation: Light is an energy transfer pathway, not a store. The 8 stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, chemical, thermal, nuclear, magnetic, electrostatic.

questions.question: A 2 kg ball is moving at 4 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
What happens to the gravitational potential energy of a ball thrown upwards?
questions.explanation: As ball rises, kinetic → GPE (increases). At top, max GPE. As falls, GPE → kinetic (decreases).

questions.question: A 50 kg student climbs a 6 m high staircase. Calculate the GPE gained. (g = 10 N/kg)
State the unit of energy.
questions.explanation: The SI unit of energy is the joule (J).

tests.name: Energy Calculations
tests.description: Work, power, efficiency, and specific heat capacity calculations

questions.question: A force of 20 N moves an object 5 m. Work done?
A motor does 500 J of work in 10 s. What is its power?
A kettle uses 200,000 J of energy. 160,000 J heats the water. Efficiency?
0.5 kg of water is heated from 20°C to 80°C. Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg°C. Calculate energy transferred.
How can you reduce unwanted energy transfer by friction?
questions.explanation: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts.

tests.name: Exam Practice
tests.description: Mixed exam questions including 6-marker on efficiency

questions.question: A spring with k = 200 N/m is stretched 0.1 m. Elastic potential energy?
Which energy resource is renewable?
questions.explanation: Wind is renewable. Coal, gas are fossil fuels (non-renewable). Nuclear uses uranium (finite).

questions.question: A student investigates the efficiency of a motor lifting a 2 kg mass through 1.5 m. The motor uses 50 J of electrical energy. Calculate the efficiency of the motor. (g = 10 N/kg)
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of using wind turbines vs coal power stations for generating electricity.
questions.correctAnswer: Wind: renewable, zero CO₂ in operation, low running costs. Disadvantages: intermittent, visual/noise impact, high setup cost. Coal: reliable, high energy density, existing infrastructure. Disadvantages: CO₂ emissions, air pollution, finite resource, mining damage.
questions.explanation: Wind: pros - renewable, clean, low running costs. Cons - intermittent, visual impact, high capital cost. Coal: pros - reliable, energy dense, existing grid. Cons - CO₂, pollution, finite, mining damage.
